The term **regioner** refers to the five administrative regions of Denmark: Hovedstaden, Sjælland, Syddanmark, Midtjylland, and Nordjylland. In the context of the national healthcare quality monitoring system, these regions serve as the primary geographical stratification level for analyzing and reporting healthcare indicators. 

Specifically, the regions are used to stratify data for [[indikator-7|Indikator 7]], a national quality indicator that tracks the incidence of [[alvorlig-bloedning|Alvorlig blødning]] (severe bleeding) among patients with atrial fibrillation undergoing anticoagulation treatment [^src1]. This regional breakdown allows health authorities to monitor the safety of treatments across different parts of the country, complementing national and local health cluster data [^src1]. 

When analyzing the data at the regional level, the proportion of patients admitted with severe bleeding was found to vary narrowly between 2.1% and 2.3% across the different regions [^src1]. The raw data highlights the distribution of these events, showing figures such as 830 events out of 38,830 in Hovedstaden, 523 out of 23,101 in Sjælland, 717 out of 31,414 in Syddanmark, 674 out of 30,615 in Midtjylland, and 348 out of 14,929 in Nordjylland, compared to the national total of 3,092 out of 138,889 [^src1].
